# Brian Phillips — Autonomous CTO

> Brian Phillips helps founders and operators establish the truth about stalled,
> expensive, or provider-dependent software delivery, then build a client-controlled
> operating foundation when the evidence supports it.

## Primary offer: Engineering Rescue Audit

- Fixed fee: $12,500 USD
- Duration: 2–3 weeks
- Mode: independent and read-only by default
- Audience: leaders with a real software product, material operating dependence,
  and unresolved questions about ownership, delivery, cost, risk, or continuity

The audit examines company control of repositories, cloud accounts, domains,
credentials, signing identities, delivery workflows, monitoring, vendor
dependencies, costs, and operating knowledge. Leadership receives an executive
risk briefing, ownership and access map, evidence-backed findings, and a
prioritized 90-day roadmap.

The audit is not an exhaustive code review, penetration test, legal opinion,
financial audit, vendor-dispute service, or guarantee of a predetermined result.
The client is not obligated to hire Brian for implementation afterward.

## Possible work after the audit

1. Foundation Build — $45,000–$75,000 fixed fee, generally 8–12 weeks
2. Autonomous Operations — $4,000–$8,000 per month after the foundation is proven

These phases are proposed only when supported by the audit findings. Pricing is
an indicative public range, not a promise that every situation fits the offer.

## Operating principles

- The client controls infrastructure, accounts, delivery workflows, technical
  memory, documentation, and handoff materials.
- Recommendations identify evidence, business consequence, confidence, owner,
  timing, and approval requirements.
- Humans retain approval over production, money, identity, data, security, legal,
  and destructive decisions.
- Automation must be observable, testable, reversible, and bounded.
- The engagement is built for succession, including a usable operating record and exit.

## Brian Phillips

Brian has 15+ years across engineering leadership, mobile and full-stack
development, infrastructure, delivery operations, vendor transitions, and
open-source software. Publicly represented work contexts include Tommy Car Wash
Systems, Nike, Amazon, Toyota, PepsiCo, NAV Canada, IBM, and Rigetti. He has
maintained and contributed to MAVSDK-Swift.
